identity: A position identity is (account, normalized symbol). For live mainnet Binance the account is the exchange account UID from the signed read-only account endpoint (shared by every key pair of one account, fail-closed); for testnet and other venues it is the API credential pair the order is signed with.

entries.mechanism: POST /trade and /trade/async never consulted the bot registry: on a live server with server keys an authenticated manual trade placed OrderLive orders on a symbol a running bot owned, so the bot and the operator acted on one position concurrently.
entries.witness: Model mutant unguarded-manual: bot t1 on account A running while a manual trade on account A is acting.
entries.resolution: runManualTrade holds a claim on the identity for the whole trade (admitted under the runtime lock only if no live bot owns it, else HTTP 409), and bot start publication refuses a claimed identity. Close-position stays an explicit reduce-only operator override. /trade/async refuses with 409 before queuing when a live bot already owns the identity; the in-job claim stays authoritative for a bot that starts in between, which the job then reports as its error.

entries.mechanism: The bot registry is unique per (tenant key, symbol). Without request keys a tenant key comes from the X-Tenant-Key header, so two bot starts with different headers could both run one symbol on the server account.
entries.witness: Model mutant tenant-keyed: bots t1 and t2, both on account A, running at once.
entries.resolution: Each live-capable bot records its owner identity; bot start publication refuses an identity owned by any tenant's bot. A bot with tradeEnabled and live Binance args owns its identity even when dryRun is set, because the bot order path ignores dryRun.
